entry.question:
## Physical scenario

This problem involves analyzing a heat engine that follows a closed cycle on a $p$-$V$ diagram.

## Question

What is the thermal efficiency for the heat engine shown in figure?

## Answer choices

- A: A: 0.74

- B: B: 0.33

- C: C: 0.912

- D: D: 0.088

## Figure caption (auxiliary; use the image as primary evidence)

The image is a pressure-volume (p-V) diagram featuring a closed cycle represented by a triangular path made up of three straight lines connecting points on the graph. The axes are labeled with \( p \) (pressure, in kPa) on the vertical axis and \( V \) (volume, in cm³) on the horizontal axis. 

- The horizontal axis ranges from 0 to 200 cm³, and the vertical axis ranges from 0 to 500 kPa.
- The three vertices of the triangle are connected by arrows, indicating the direction of the process cycle:
  - The first arrow points right, indicating an increase in volume at constant pressure.
  - The second arrow points downwards, indicating a decrease in pressure at constant volume.
  - The third arrow points diagonally back to the starting point.

There are two purple arrows indicating heat transfer:
- An arrow labeled “\( Q = 30 \, \text{J} \)” is directed towards the path at the lower left.
- Another arrow labeled “\( Q = 84 \, \text{J} \)” is directed towards the path at the upper part.

These labels suggest energy transfers into the system as heat during certain parts of the cycle.
